<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518914548_theRebbe_632" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518914548_theRebbe_632__p004">
  <section v="9">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>These three aspects also apply to the teshuvah of returning the sparks to their source.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, these three matters mentioned above also apply to the teshuvah of returning the sparks</t>
    <t s="2">(that are in physical things)</t>
    <t s="3">to their source,</t>
    <t s="4">for in this teshuvah as well there is a parallel to the three matters above.</t>
    <t s="5">First,</t>
    <t s="6">the thirst and longing of the sparks</t>
    <t s="7">(from the perspective of their root)</t>
    <t s="8">to ascend from their descent and return to their source,</t>
    <t s="9">like the lower waters that weep, saying, "We desire to be before the King."</t>
    <t s="10">Second,</t>
    <t s="11">the great joy that results from the elevation of the sparks and their return to their source after having been distanced.</t>
    <t s="12">And third,</t>
    <t s="13">since the sparks that fell into the shells,</t>
    <t s="14">even into the shell of Nogah,</t>
    <t s="15">had their light extinguished,</t>
    <t s="16">therefore, from the perspective of their state, it is not possible for them to be refined and elevated to their root,</t>
    <t s="17">and when they are refined and ascend to their root</t>
    <t s="18">(through the service of man),</t>
    <t s="19">it is a novelty.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="10">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The novelty in the teshuvah of returning sparks is greater than the novelty in simple teshuvah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it can be said</t>
    <t s="1">that the novelty in the teshuvah of returning the sparks is a greater novelty than the novelty in simple teshuvah.</t>
    <t s="2">For in simple teshuvah,</t>
    <t s="3">even though before teshuvah he was in a state where he did not do the will of the Holy One, blessed be He, as above,</t>
    <t s="4">this is only as it is in externality,</t>
    <t s="5">but his true will</t>
    <t s="6">(even then)</t>
    <t s="7">was to fulfill the will of his Creator</t>
    <t s="8">(as per the well-known ruling),</t>
    <t s="9">except that this will was in a state of extreme concealment,</t>
    <t s="10">to the extent that its revelation is like a novelty.</t>
    <t s="11">However, this is not the case with the teshuvah of returning the sparks to their source,</t>
    <t s="12">for since the sparks that fell into the shells</t>
    <t s="13">(even into the shell of Nogah)</t>
    <t s="14">had their light darkened,</t>
    <t s="15">to the point that they are not in the category of light at all,</t>
    <t s="16">their refinement and elevation is a true novelty.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="11">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The advantage of thirst from distance is primarily in the teshuvah of the soul, while the joy from closeness of sparks is like that of two friends.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">However,</t>
    <t s="2">this matter</t>
    <t s="3">(the superiority in the teshuvah of returning the sparks)</t>
    <t s="4">is in the quality of the novelty in teshuvah.</t>
    <t s="5">But the quality of the thirst that comes from distance is primarily in the teshuvah of the soul</t>
    <t s="6">(both in the teshuvah of the righteous and in simple teshuvah).</t>
    <t s="7">For since the connection of souls with G-dliness is an intrinsic connection,</t>
    <t s="8">like the connection of a son with his father</t>
    <t s="9">("You are children to the L-rd your G-d")</t>
    <t s="10">which is an intrinsic connection,</t>
    <t s="11">therefore, when the soul feels that it is distant from G-dliness</t>
    <t s="12">(the distance caused by its descent below,</t>
    <t s="13">and certainly the distance caused by sins),</t>
    <t s="14">this touches its very essence,</t>
    <t s="15">and consequently,</t>
    <t s="16">the thirst caused by the feeling of distance also touches its essence.</t>
    <t s="17">And so too regarding the delight from the closeness that comes after the distance,</t>
    <t s="18">for since souls are children,</t>
    <t s="19">for a son is from the very essence of the father,</t>
    <t s="20">the delight of the father from his son drawing near</t>
    <t s="21">(after having been distanced),</t>
    <t s="22">and all the more so his only son,</t>
    <t s="23">is an essential delight.</t>
    <t s="24">However, the delight from the closeness of the sparks after they have been distanced is like that of two friends</t>
    <t s="25">who have not seen each other for a long time, and when they draw near and see each other,</t>
    <t s="26">they delight and rejoice greatly,</t>
    <t s="27">a delight which,</t>
    <t s="28">(though it is a great delight),</t>
    <t s="29">is like other delights that come from something external to oneself.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
